extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), USPTO examiners, and disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules governing practitioner conduct before the USPTO, the permissibility of third‑party filings in patent applications, and related disciplinary consequences. Focuses on when filings in another's application are authorized and what constitutes improper purpose or inadequate preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.133(g) and 10.159. Proceedings filed before September 15, 2008 are governed by Part 10 of 37 C.F.R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the statutory/regulatory bases for OED disciplinary authority and which regulatory scheme applies based on filing date of the complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO not forum for ownership disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: It is well settled that a USPTO patent application proceeding is not the appropriate forum for resolving a dispute concerning ownership of the application, and, as such, the Office will not permit itself to become embroiled in ownership disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites precedents (Ex Parte Harrison; In re Moller; Ex Parte McTammany; Ex Parte McFarlane; Ex Parte Gallatin) and is the foundational principle for rejecting attempts by third parties to alter inventorship or ownership in ex parte proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No third‑party right to intervene in prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party has no right to intervene in the prosecution of another's patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After publication, a third party is permitted to submit only patents and publications within two months of publication or prior to mailing of a notice of allowance, whichever is earlier, and must serve such filing on the attorney of record (37 C.F.R. § 1.99; 35 U.S.C. § 122(c)). The rules do not permit a third party to petition the Office to withdraw an application from issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on third‑party submissions (37 C.F.R. § 1.99)
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties may submit only patents and publications within the two‑month window after publication (or prior to notice of allowance) and must serve the submission on the attorney of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions beyond this narrow allowance are not permitted and attempting broader filings in a published application can be improper and untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing on behalf of a party without standing is an improper purpose (37 C.F.R. § 10.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO considers the filing of a petition or other paper on behalf of a party having no standing in an application, and not otherwise authorized by the patent rules of practice, to be a petition or paper presented for an improper purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: filing on behalf of a third party to extinguish the applicant's rights or intervene in the application. Such filings delay examination/processing and may be referred to OED for disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPEP is guidance, not law
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP provides instructions and information for examiners and practitioners but does not have the force of law or the force of the rules in Title 37 of the Code of Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP § 402.10 and § 201.03 are cited as guidance (e.g., on power-of-attorney signature requirements and inventor declarations), but failure to follow MPEP practices may still result in rejection unless the underlying regulation/statute permits otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration requirement for inventors (37 C.F.R. § 1.63 / MPEP § 201.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration under 37 C.F.R. § 1.63 by each actual inventor must be presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to correct inventorship or an amendment that lacks an appropriate oath/declaration is 'facially not grantable.' Filings attempting to add inventors without the required inventor statements will be dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. § 116 and third‑party limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. § 116 does not state or imply that a third party is authorized to file a change in inventorship in another person's application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the named applicant/inventor does not agree that others are inventors, the correction procedures under § 1.48 are not available to a third party; a third party cannot unilaterally add themselves as inventors in another's application based on § 116.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions of 37 C.F.R. § 1.48(a) for correcting inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 1.48(a) sets out conditions to correct inventorship, which were interpreted by the USPTO as not permitting a third party to add themselves absent required consents/conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should confirm that the specific regulatory conditions are met (including any required signatures/consents or petitions with good and sufficient reasons) before submitting a § 1.48 amendment; relying on a novel interpretation is risky.

rubrics_metrics.name: A third party cannot petition to withdraw application from issue
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules of patent practice do not permit a third party to petition the Office to withdraw an application from issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions to withdraw from issue and requests for continued examination (e.g., under 37 C.F.R. § 1.313) are not available as a means for a third party to delay issuance or insert themselves into prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to serve filings on the applicant/attorney contemporaneously (best practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners should provide the applicant or the applicant's attorney with a copy of filings contemporaneously with submitting them to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relying solely on PAIR posting is not sufficient practice; the respondent acknowledged that better practice would have been to serve the applicant or their counsel when submitting filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot unilaterally diminish applicant's property rights in ex parte matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not permit a practitioner to unilaterally, and in an ex parte matter, diminish an applicant's property rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners and the Office will reject attempts that would extinguish or alter an applicant's rights without proper authorization or opposing party participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling a matter without adequate preparation violates professional conduct (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling a legal matter without preparation adequate in the circumstances constitutes a violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard was the admitted violation forming the basis for public reprimand in the case; practitioners must research and ensure competence regarding regulatory requirements before taking novel or potentially disallowed actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible disciplinary consequences and remedial actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary sanctions may include public reprimand, publication of the Final Order and Notice of Reprimand (Official Gazette), notice to disciplinary agencies/courts, motions to dismiss pending proceedings, and allocation of costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agreed sanctions here included public reprimand, publication, notice to state disciplinary agencies/courts, filing a motion to dismiss the pending complaint, and each party bearing their own costs; OED may refer third‑party misuse to disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party attempts to protest/oppose grant may be referred to OED
rubrics_metrics.description: Filings by a third party in published applications other than those expressly permitted under § 1.99 may be referred to OED for appropriate disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official Gazette reference: 'Third Party Attempts to Protest or Otherwise Oppose the Grant of a Published Application' (Official Gazette, April 22, 2003). Such attempts are closely scrutinized and can trigger enforcement.
